question.:question/problem:
Determine whether the following system of equations is consistent or inconsistent. If it is consistent, indicate whether it is consistent dependent or consistent independent.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x - y - 6 &=0 \\ -6x + 5y &=-16\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x - y - 6 &= 0 \\ 2x &= 6 + y \\ x &= 3 + \frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=3 + \frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6x + 5y &= -16 \\ -6\left(3 + \frac{1}{2}y\right) + 5y &= -16 \\ -18 - 3y + 5y &= -16 \\ 2y &= 2 \\ y &= 1\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a single value of $y$, and $x$ is determined by $x=3 + \frac{1}{2}y$, there is exactly one solution to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent independent.

question.:question/problem:
Determine whether the following system of equations is consistent or inconsistent. If it is consistent, indicate whether it is consistent dependent or consistent independent.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}6x + 6y - 6 &=0 \\ 12x + 12y &=12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x + 6y - 6 &= 0 \\ 6x &= 6 - 6y \\ x &= 1 - y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=1 - y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}12x + 12y &= 12 \\ 12\left(1 - y\right) + 12y &= 12 \\ 12 - 12y + 12y &= 12 \\ 12 &= 12\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a true statement, we conclude that there are infinitely many solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent dependent.

Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}6x - 3y &=-3 \\ -2x + y &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x - 3y &= -3 \\ 6x &= -3 + 3y \\ x &= -\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x + y &= 1 \\ -2\left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}y\right) + y &= 1 \\ 1 - y + y &= 1 \\ 1 &= 1\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a true statement, we conclude that there are infinitely many solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent dependent.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}6x &=4 + 2y \\ 3y &=9 - 12x\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x &= 4 + 2y \\ x &= \frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y &= 9 - 12x \\ 3y &= 9 - 12\left(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}y\right) \\ 3y &= 9 - 8 - 4y \\ 7y &= 1 \\ y &= \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a single value of $y$, and $x$ is determined by $x=\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}y$, there is exactly one solution to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent independent.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x - 3y &=-9 \\ -4x - 6y &=-18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x - 3y &= -9 \\ -2x &= -9 + 3y \\ x &= \frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x - 6y &= -18 \\ -4\left(\frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\right) - 6y &= -18 \\ -18 + 6y - 6y &= -18 \\ -18 &= -18\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a true statement, we conclude that there are infinitely many solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent dependent.
